title: Animosis release manifest
description: The signed document a patcher fetches to learn what a channel currently contains. It is the ONLY document that is signed; every artifact is authenticated by a SHA-256 recorded here, so one signature covers the whole release. See docs/patcher-protocol.md.

schema.description: Manifest format version. A patcher that does not know this value must refuse the manifest and tell the user to update, never guess.

channel.description: Channels are independent timelines. A 'serial' is only comparable within one channel.

version.description: Human-facing release version. Display only — ordering decisions use 'serial'.

serial.description: Monotonically increasing within a channel. A client MUST refuse a manifest whose serial is lower than the highest it has accepted, which is what stops an attacker replaying an old signed manifest to force a downgrade onto a patched vulnerability. Never reuse or reorder a serial.

released.description: Informational only. Clocks are attacker-influenced and skew legitimately; 'serial' is the ordering authority.

minPatcher.description: Oldest patcher that can apply this release. A patcher below this MUST self-update before touching any package.

baseUrl.description: Artifact URLs resolve against this. Keeping it here rather than in each artifact means a CDN move is one line, and the signed document stays portable. HTTPS is mandatory: TLS is not the integrity guarantee (the signature is) but it stops passive observation of what a user is installing.

notes.description: Release notes URL, opened in the user's browser — never rendered inside the patcher, which would make signed-but-hostile HTML an attack surface.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex. Verified over the bytes as downloaded, before any decompression — a decompressor fed unverified input is a parser fed attacker data.

url.description: Resolved against baseUrl. Relative, and MUST NOT contain '..' or a leading '/' — a client rejects the manifest outright if it does.

size.description: Exact byte count. Used for the progress bar AND as a hard cap: a client stops reading once it exceeds this, so a hostile CDN cannot stream an unbounded body at a disk.

unpackedSize.description: Bytes after decompression. Checked against free disk space before starting, and enforced during unpack to bound decompression bombs.

from.description: The installed version this patch applies to. A client uses a delta ONLY when its recorded local version matches exactly.

format.description: zstd --patch-from. Zstandard is BSD-3-Clause (dual GPLv2; take BSD-3) — no commercial restriction, no patent grant needed.

sha256.description: Hash of the patch file itself.

resultSha256.description: Hash of the artifact AFTER the patch is applied. Non-negotiable: it must equal the full artifact's sha256, which is what proves the delta path and the full-download path converge on identical bytes. Mismatch means discard and fall back to the full download.

id.description: Reverse-dotted, e.g. 'animosis.core', 'animosis.terrain'. Stable forever — this is the identity the local state file keys on.

required.description: false marks an optional component the user can decline (sample content, debug symbols).

installPath.description: Destination relative to the install root. Must not escape it: no leading '/', no '..'. Enforced by the client, not trusted from here.

dependsOn.description: Package ids that must be installed at or above their listed version first. The graph must be acyclic; a client that detects a cycle refuses the manifest.

deltas.description: Optional fast paths. Every delta is an optimisation only — the full artifact must always remain downloadable, so a client can always recover.
